name: The Worker · Job Help, Work Clothing and Housing

informationText.before:
**Programs and Services**
Free job planning, employer referrals, resumes, interview preparation and interview clothing. Uniforms, safety shoes, tools and transportation help may be available; ask about the items and limits.

The separate Workforce Housing program offers 90 days in a private room in shared housing, weekly support and life-skills classes, followed by nine months of follow-up.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Job-search services are free for unemployed or underemployed people. Newly employed assistance generally requires permanent/direct-hire W-2 work, 25–40 hours weekly, at least minimum wage and a start within the past 30 days. Required screenings must be completed. Temporary, seasonal, staffing-agency and app-based jobs do not qualify for that extra assistance.

Workforce Housing has separate rules: applicants must work full time in a direct-hire job earning at least $18 an hour. Ask about current openings and any other requirements; qualifying for job-search help does not qualify someone for housing.

**How to Best Connect**
Walk into 1833 W. Main St., Suite 128, Mesa, Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–noon or 1–4 p.m.; closed noon–1 p.m. No appointment is needed. Call 602-755-5627 with questions. Bring photo ID, a phone and a resume if available; ask for help if these are missing.

**Access**
The office is near the Sycamore/Main Street light-rail stop. For newly employed assistance, have the employer email jobs@theworkeraz.org from a company address with your full name, start date, pay and weekly hours. This is separate from starting a job search. For Workforce Housing, ask a housing expert about enrollment, the waiting list, housing location and costs. The Mesa office is not a housing unit.

**Important Information to Know**
The newly employed resources are offered once and depend on supplies. Ask staff which clothing or equipment they can provide before purchasing it. The organization also uses the name St. Joseph the Worker. Housing is a separate program. The site describes low living costs but gives no current amount; ask about rent, deposits and other charges before agreeing to a place. Do not assume the free job-search service means free housing.

You need 30–45 days on the job or at least two pay stubs, must save 80% of net pay, attend weekly meetings and take life-skills workshops during the first 30 days. Some felony histories are considered individually. These rules are separate from job-search and new-job assistance.

Walk into 1833 W. Main St., Suite 128, Mesa, Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–noon or 1–4 p.m.; closed noon–1 p.m. No appointment is needed. Call 602-755-5627 with questions. Bring photo ID, a phone and a resume if available; ask for help if these are missing.

**Access**
The office is near the Sycamore/Main Street light-rail stop. For newly employed assistance, have the employer email jobs@theworkeraz.org from a company address with your full name, start date, pay and weekly hours. This is separate from starting a job search. For Workforce Housing, ask a housing expert about enrollment, the waiting list, housing location and costs. The Mesa office is not a housing unit.

**Important Information to Know**
The newly employed resources are offered once and depend on supplies. Ask staff which clothing or equipment they can provide before purchasing it. The organization also uses the name St. Joseph the Worker. Housing is a separate program. The site describes low living costs but gives no current amount; ask about rent, deposits and other charges before agreeing to a place. Do not assume the free job-search service means free housing. The housing page currently estimates a 2–3 month wait and sets a savings goal of at least $5,000 by program completion. Confirm the wait when applying; this is not immediate shelter.

name: La Mesa Ministries · Clothing, Meals, IDs, Benefits and Bus Passes

name.before: La Mesa Ministries · Documents, Mail, Benefits and Bus Passes
name.after: La Mesa Ministries · Clothing, Meals, IDs, Benefits and Bus Passes

description.before: One-on-one help with documents, benefit forms and mail in Mesa. Free daily bus passes are offered at separate weekly gatherings; call about help reaching an interview or medical appointment.
description.after: Clothing, meals and daily bus passes at weekly gatherings, plus help with IDs, mail and benefit applications at the Mesa Resource Center.

informationText.before:
**Programs and Services**
Help applying for IDs, driver licenses, birth certificates, Social Security cards and federal benefits. Staff assist with forms, appointments and service connections. Mail service is available for people who cannot afford a post office box.

Weekly gatherings offer meals, clothing, hygiene supplies and free daily bus passes.

**Eligibility Requirements**
La Mesa focuses on people experiencing homelessness and the working poor. Detailed document-service eligibility is not published. Call even if records are missing; explain what you have and ask what staff can help obtain.

The gatherings welcome everyone. No ID or income requirement for passes is published; ask about the specific ride or item needed.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-590-4622 for the Resource Center at 805 N. Country Club Dr. It is open Tuesday–Thursday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; appointments are suggested. Say which document or benefit application you need help with.

Bus passes: Tuesday, 4:30–6 p.m., at First Christian Church, 805 N. Country Club Dr., Mesa; Thursday at Beautiful Savior Lutheran Church, 1337 W. 11th St., Tempe, at the same time. Call to check supply. For appointment-ride help, give the Resource Center your destination and appointment time; info@lamesaministries.org also accepts appointment requests.

**Access**
In Mesa at First Christian Church. Ask about help reaching an interview or medical appointment. Free daily bus passes are also distributed at the Tuesday Mesa and Thursday Tempe gatherings, 4:30–6 p.m.; these are separate from office hours.

**Important Information to Know**
Ask whether document fees can be covered and whether staff can obtain records from your birth state. A four-week financial class starts the first Tuesday each month at 5:30 p.m. Graduates can work with a housing counselor; move-in help and furniture depend on qualification. Recovery sponsorship connects people with outside faith-based programs.

A daily pass is not continuing transit funding. Rides are not a daily shuttle or guaranteed same-day service; confirm arrangements and any cost. Gathering meals start at 6 p.m.; worship at 6:30 is optional.

name: Streets of Joy · Food, Clothing, Hygiene and School Supplies

informationText.before:
**Programs and Services**
Clothing and shoes for everyday wear, work and school, along with hygiene products and school supplies. The separate Food Center offers food boxes while supplies last.

**Eligibility Requirements**
The center describes help for veterans, its program residents, people experiencing homelessness and low-income families. Ask about any requirements for the items you need. The food-box page lists no eligibility requirements and says first come, first served; ask about the current process when calling.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-757-6921 first. Say whether you need food, clothing or other supplies, and ask staff to confirm current service and pickup arrangements. For clothing, give sizes and say whether you are a Streets of Joy resident. Email: info@streetsofjoy.com.

**Access**
451 E. 4th Pl., Mesa. The food page lists Wednesday 2–4 PM and Saturday 1–4 PM; confirm before traveling. Clothing pickup hours may be different. Ask whether clothing needs an appointment or referral.

**Important Information to Know**
Supplies and sizes vary. Ask about any cost, documents and limits on repeat visits when arranging pickup.
